x-interview.ask: Who is the book for — a reader age band, or general/all-ages?

style.description: Short human-readable illustration style label, e.g. 'soft watercolor, pastel palette'. Used in prose (image_prompts mention it) and as a quick summary; the paid scripts inject 'style_guide' (required) into every API call, not this field. When the user supplies a style reference image (an illustration or screenshot showing the desired look), view it in-session with the Read tool and derive both 'style' and 'style_guide' from what you see — the image is analyzed in-session, not persisted or passed to the renderer.

x-interview.ask: What illustration style? E.g. soft watercolor (default), bold flat cartoon, anime/cel-shaded, pixel art, caricature, comic-book, colored-pencil, paper-cutout collage — describe your own, or share a style reference image to match.

style_guide.description: REQUIRED structured style guide. The render and stylesheet scripts assemble a single deterministic style block from these fields (in fixed order: medium → palette → line → lighting → mood) and inject it byte-identically into every API call. This locks book-wide visual consistency — each page is a separate stateless API call, and having the exact same verbatim block in every prompt is the documented consistency mechanism (per Google's Book_illustration workflow). Both paid scripts refuse to run when this object is missing or empty. At least one field must be set.

medium.description: Rendering medium and technique, e.g. 'soft watercolor with pen-and-ink outline'.

palette.description: 3–5 named or hex color swatches that define the book's palette, e.g. ['warm cream #F5E9D4', 'sage green #8FAF85', 'dusty coral #E8917A']. These are injected verbatim — the more specific, the better the cross-page consistency.

line.description: Line-work description, e.g. 'thin sepia ink, even weight, rounded corners'.

lighting.description: Lighting direction, quality, and color temperature, e.g. 'golden-hour side-light, long shadows' or 'flat even light, no gradients'.

mood.description: Overall mood and rendering vocabulary, e.g. 'cozy and gentle' or 'graphic, high-contrast, irreverent'.

style_frame.description: Path to the book-wide 'style frame' PNG (PER-82, Lever B) — filled in by make_style_sheet.py, not user-authored. An abstract style board (palette swatches, a line/texture sample, a lighting study; no characters, no places, no scenery) sent as the lowest-priority reference on every Stage 3 page render call to anchor the look of everything that isn't cast. Omit for no style frame — Stage 2 always attempts to generate one once per book.

cast.description: Explicit unified cast: every recurring visual subject in the book — characters, recognisable objects, and named places. ONE entry per REAL subject. Drives Stage 2 (one reference sheet per eligible entry) and Stage 3 (per-page reference selection). Never rely on auto-extraction from prose.

id.description: Stable lowercase identifier for this cast entry. Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ (e.g. 'pip', 'major-oak'). Referenced by pages[].cast and <id> placeholders in image_prompt. Also the style-sheet filename slug (style-sheet-{id}.png). NEVER reaches the image model — render resolves <id> → name before the Gemini call. Stable across display-name renames.

name.description: Human-readable display name shown to the image model (e.g. 'Pip', 'Major Oak'). Used in Gemini-facing prompt substitutions and reference-image labels.

kind.description: What this entry is. 'character' (default): person or creature — gets a style sheet; the outfit lock applies; eligible to be a page hero (first character-kind entry in pages[].cast — leads reference ordering into the cap). 'object': recurring prop, vehicle, or item — gets a reference sheet with multi-angle/detail-close-up prompt. 'location': a named place — gets a location reference sheet generated in Stage 2 from its real-place photo(s) in ref_image (downloaded in Stage 1) plus 'appearance'; without ref_image the sheet comes from 'appearance' alone (fictional recurring place). At render time the sheet is the reference (lowest cap priority); the raw photo is the fallback when no sheet exists.

appearance.description: Concrete visual description. character: species, age, hair, ONE specific outfit/clothing, colours, distinguishing features — the outfit named here becomes the character's canonical outfit locked into the style sheet and worn unchanged on every page (name exactly one outfit; more specific = more consistent). object: shape, size, colours, materials, distinguishing details. location: terrain/architecture, vegetation, landmarks, atmosphere — feeds the sheet prompt (alongside any ref_image photos).

ref_image.description: Optional reference photo(s). kind=character: a single absolute path or an array of paths (e.g. multiple angles of the same person); used for face and hair likeness only — clothing/outfit always comes from 'appearance', not these photos; capped at 5 (Gemini 3 Pro Image character-lane limit). kind=object: photo(s) of the object (single path or array); shape/colour/detail reference; capped at 5. kind=location: real-place photo(s) produced by fetch_location.py — an array of paths (loc-{slug}-1.jpg, loc-{slug}-2.jpg, …); target 3 distinct angles/views, minimum 1 (a plain string is also accepted); Stage 2 generates the location style sheet from these photos; capped at 5.

style_sheet.description: Path to this entry's generated reference sheet PNG (filled in by make_style_sheet.py — every cast entry, all kinds).

source_url.description: Optional provenance for downloaded reference photo(s) (prefer the Wikimedia Commons file page — it carries license and attribution). A single URL, or an array parallel to ref_image: one file-page URL per downloaded photo, same order. Relevant for kind=location entries whose ref_image files were produced by fetch_location.py.

text_mode.description: How page text is rendered. 'native' (default): ask the image model to render the story text directly into the illustration (output goes to page-NN-native.png). 'overlay': generate image with a text-safe zone, then Pillow-composite text via overlay_text.py. 'long': each body page becomes two physical pages — (1) full-bleed art with no text (pages/page-NN-long.png), (2) a separate text-only page with the story text on a centered, feathered semi-transparent panel over ONE shared model-generated background reused book-wide (pages/text-bg-long.png; designed with a reserved low-detail central text area). Cover (page 1) stays a single combined overlay-style page. Cost = N art calls + 1 shared-background call; a page with 'text_background_prompt' gets its own dedicated background instead (+1 call for that page). render_book.py's --text-mode flag overrides this per run. A page-level 'text_mode' field overrides this for that specific page (see pages[].text_mode).

x-interview.ask: How should the story text appear on the pages? 'long' suits text-heavy books (~80+ words per spread).

text_background_prompt.description: Used when any page's effective text mode is 'long'. Optional custom scene description for the book's shared text-page background (pages/text-bg-long.png — one model-generated image reused on every text page; the book style block is injected, no character references are sent, and a low-detail central area is reserved for text). Omit for a generic style-matched decorative background. Ignored when no page renders in long mode.

premise.description: Optional book-wide narrative anchor injected verbatim into EVERY page render prompt (render-only, Stage 3) — the textual analogue of the style block. Describe ABSTRACT atmosphere/intent ONLY: genre, target audience age, overall tone, season, time-of-day arc, narrative register. NEVER plot, scenes, named places, or per-page objects — anything page-specific bleeds into every page (the PER-33 location-bleed bug). Rule of thumb: if a phrase names a thing that should appear on some pages but not others, it's plot — move it to that page's image_prompt. Answers 'what kind of book is this?', never 'what happens?'. Not injected into style sheets (Stage 2) or the long-mode text background. Omit for no change.

x-interview.ask: One-line book-wide narrative tone/atmosphere (genre, audience age, mood) — abstract only, no plot or places.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language tag for the book text (e.g. 'en', 'de', 'en-GB'). Used as dc:language metadata in EPUB output (Stage 4, storybook-consolidate). Default: 'en'.

x-interview.ask: Book language (BCP-47 tag, e.g. en, de).

fonts.description: Optional book-wide map of text role -> font family name. Defines which font each per-page 'font' role uses. Values are family names (e.g. 'Arial', 'Patrick Hand') resolved at render time: bundled asset in assets/fonts/ -> system-installed font -> bundled role default. Omit to use the bundled Andika (reader) / PatrickHand (display).

x-interview.ask: Custom fonts for body text (reader) and titles (display); bundled Andika / Patrick Hand by default.

display.description: Title/cover font family. Default: Patrick Hand (bundled).

resolution.description: Optional book-wide image resolution for page rendering. 2K (default) is good for screen and print up to ~8×8 in; 1K is faster/cheaper for drafts; 4K for large-format print. The render CLI --resolution flag overrides this value when passed explicitly.

x-interview.ask: Render quality vs cost — 1K draft / 2K standard / 4K large-format print.

aspect_ratio.description: Optional book-wide aspect ratio applied to both style sheets and page renders. When omitted, the model picks framing on each call (non-deterministic). Set this to lock consistent framing across all sheets and pages (e.g. '4:3' for landscape, '3:4' for portrait, '1:1' for square). The stylesheet/render CLI --aspect-ratio flag overrides this value when passed explicitly.

x-interview.ask: Lock one page framing for the whole book, or leave unset to let the model choose per page.

model.description: Optional book-wide image model for page rendering (Stage 3 only — style sheets always use gemini-3-pro-image). References ride two lanes (character, object), and both lane caps are per-model. 'gemini-3.1-flash-image' (default): faster and cheaper, character lane up to 4, object lane up to 10. 'gemini-3-pro-image': higher quality, character lane up to 5, object lane up to 6. A page-level 'model' overrides this for that page; the render CLI --model flag overrides both for an entire run. Note: pages whose character lane exceeds 4 are automatically upgraded to gemini-3-pro-image at render time (runtime-only; story.json is never modified) — which also shrinks that page's object lane from 10 to 6.

x-interview.ask: Image model for page renders — flash (default, cheaper, 4-char/10-object cap) or pro (higher quality, 5-char/6-object cap).

saved_formats.description: Optional export hint consumed by Stage 4 (storybook-consolidate): which finished book files the user wants assembled from the rendered pages — 'pdf' (multi-page PDF) and/or 'epub' (fixed-layout EPUB3). Omitted = all formats; an empty array records a 'no book files' preference. Nothing is assembled automatically and no script reads this field — the consolidate skill uses it as the default answer when asking which formats to export, and the interactive choice always wins.

x-interview.ask: Which finished book files to export at the end (Stage 4 default — changeable at export time).

fallback_vendor.description: Optional fallback vendor for page rendering (Stage 3). When Gemini returns finish_reason=PROHIBITED_CONTENT (a deterministic content-policy block, not a transient error), render_book.py automatically retries the page on this vendor. 'openai' (default): retry on OpenAI gpt-image-2 with moderation='low', using the exact same resolved prompt and selected style sheets — only fires when STORYBOOK_SKILL_OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY is set in the environment; if no key is present the page fails as normal. 'none': disable the fallback entirely. Transient 5xx/429 Gemini errors are not affected by this setting. Precedence: render CLI --fallback-vendor flag > this field > 'openai'.

x-interview.ask: Fallback vendor when Gemini blocks a page — 'openai' (auto-retry on gpt-image-2 when key present) or 'none' (disable).

cast.description: ids of the cast entries appearing on this page — characters, objects, and locations in ONE flat list, any mix and multiplicity (e.g. ['pip', 'red-umbrella', 'gazelle-valley']). MUST match cast[].id exactly. Drives which reference images are sent when rendering this page. The FIRST entry whose kind is 'character' (or kind is absent, defaulting to character) is the page HERO — it leads reference ordering into the cap; author the hero/child first among the characters so it gets top cap priority. Characters contribute only their style sheet (no extra photo). Objects and locations follow after characters. Use [] for scenery-only or subject-free pages.

text.description: Story text for this page/spread. Empty string for cover or wordless pages.

image_prompt.description: Full image generation prompt. Reference cast members with <id> placeholders (e.g. '<pip> shelters under <major-oak>') — render resolves each <id> to the cast entry's display name before the Gemini call, so the model always sees real names. Never repeat a cast member's appearance prose (PER-42 name-only rule: the style sheet defines appearance; name-only is the stronger consistency signal). Pose, action, expression, and scene description stay in the prompt. Must mention the illustration style. Content only — do not include text-position or safe-zone directives; the render script appends those transparently from text_placement.

text_placement.description: Optional. Where text lands on the image. 'floating' (default, only meaningful when effective text mode is 'native'): the image model picks the most visually pleasing placement; the overlay path degrades this to 'bottom'. 'top'/'bottom': pin text to a fixed band. Has no effect on long-mode body pages (text goes to its own page); still honored for the long-mode cover (page 1).

text_color_hint.description: Optional text colour scheme. 'dark': near-black ink on a light semi-transparent panel (overlay/long) or warm dark ink baked in (native). 'light': near-white ink on a dark panel (overlay/long) or cream-white ink with a dark backdrop area (native). Default: dark.

text_align.description: Horizontal alignment of the overlay text. Default: left. Use 'center' for cover/title pages.

font.description: Font for the text overlay. 'reader' (Andika, body text) or 'display' (PatrickHand, titles/cover). Default: reader.

model.description: Optional per-page image model override. Unset = inherit the book-level 'model' field (or gemini-3.1-flash-image default). Set to 'gemini-3-pro-image' to retry a specific page on the stronger model without re-rendering the whole book. Also raises that page's reference-image cap from 4 to 5. Note: pages whose reference list exceeds 4 are automatically upgraded to gemini-3-pro-image at render time regardless of this field (runtime-only; story.json is never modified).

text_mode.description: Optional per-page text mode override. Unset = inherit the book-level 'text_mode' field (or 'native' default). Lets individual pages differ from the book's default mode — e.g. a single long-mode page in an otherwise native book, or an overlay cover in a long-mode book. render_book.py's --text-mode flag overrides both the book-level and page-level fields for an entire run.

text_background_prompt.description: Only meaningful when this page's effective text mode is 'long'. When set, this page's text page gets its OWN dedicated background (pages/page-NN-long-bg.png) generated from this description via ONE extra paid Gemini call, instead of the book's shared background (the book style block is injected; no character references are sent; a low-detail central area is reserved for text). Omit to use the shared book-wide background at no extra cost. Ignored when effective mode is overlay/native, and on the cover or empty-text pages. If set on an empty-text page a warning is logged and no text page is generated.
